Be careful! You don't want to fall.
In memory of all of those dumb enough to have fallen into the ravine.
The ground gives way beneath your feet with a crack of splitting roots. Before you can step back, you're falling.

You land hard - but not on stone. A bed breaks your fall, and nothing feels broken but your pride. Dirt from the roof rains down around you, covering the blankets. Dim light filters down from the hole above, enough to see stone floors and brick walls. People built this room.
You already know the fall won't kill you. Do you want to drop back down?

Someone has been here since you fell. A rope is tied to a post beside the hole and hangs down into the dark. The earth around the edge is trampled with boot prints, far more than two men would leave, and every set leads in. None lead out.
From below comes a shout, then the ring of steel. The room under this hole is where Piwh is lying.
Don't look at me. I just sleep here. Well, I did, back when the dorm had a ceiling.
Wha- hey! HEY! Where did you come from? Did you just fall through my ceiling?

replies.text: Nice place. A bit drafty now.

message: Who am I? You're the one who just dropped into my room!
Look at this. Dirt in my blankets, and sky where the roof used to be. Graball is going to lose his mind.
The man in charge. You'll meet him soon enough.
Right. You're coming with me, and don't touch anything on the way.
Not so fast. Guests don't get the tour.

The thief pulls a dark sack over your head, and the world goes black. A hand grips your arm and steers you forward. Blind, you stumble up a flight of stairs, through a warm room that smells of cooking, then somewhere cold where every step echoes. The floor turns to soft dirt under your feet, and then there are more stairs.

The thief pushes you down onto a seat and yanks the sack off your head. You blink in the light. You are at a small round table in a stone-floored nook, in the middle of a long hall with a dirt floor. Across from you, a man sets down his mug and looks you over. He does not look pleased to be interrupted.
Boss, this one came through the dorm ceiling and landed right on my bed. There's a hole up there now. You can see the sky through it.
Through the ceiling. Through. My. Ceiling.
I know your face. You robbed one of our vaults, and now you've dropped into another. Some people never learn.
Wait. I know you. You've done work for the Guild. Then you know better than to go poking around places nobody told you about. Still, better you than a guard.
I don't know you, and you've already seen more than a stranger should. That's a problem for both of us.
So. Tell me how you got in, and don't leave anything out.

replies.text: I was walking along the ravine and the ground gave way.
I fell. That's really the whole story.

message: The ground gave way. Under the ravine. Right above my base. Wonderful. Who else knows about that hole?

replies.text: No one outside of this place, as far as I know.

message: That's not good enough. There's a man who stands at that ravine every day, staring into it. Bramver. If anyone saw that hole open up, it's him.
Go and find out what he's seen. Don't tell him about this place, and don't tell him about me.
Then you're someone who knows where we sleep, and I'd have to decide what to do about that. Talk to Bramver.
Take the stairs at the end of the hall and keep going until you come up in a cabin. The door locks behind you, so when you have news, come back the way you came in.
You seem to have a talent for it.
Stop right there. You're the one who came through the dorm ceiling, aren't you? Word travels fast down here.
Bramver. The man who watches the ravine. Why are you still standing in my office?
Graball takes a long drink of his beer and says nothing.
You're back. Do you have it?
Then why are you sitting at my table?

[While turning the clock over in his hands.] And the spare key? You put it back, didn't you? Alduan comes home, finds his door locked and his key right where he left it, and spends the rest of his life wondering if he ever owned a clock.
A robbery nobody can explain is one nobody investigates. That's how we've stayed hidden down here. Good work.
[While turning the clock over in his hands, and listening to it tick, he sets it down beside his beer.] Good. Now you're one of the people who robbed Alduan.
And Alduan's key. Hand it over. A stolen key in your pocket is a clue for anyone who searches you.
Here. A key to the cabin door. I'm not saying I trust you, but I trust you more than I did.
Here. A key to the cabin door. You've done a job for me now, so you can come and go like the rest of my crew.
Here. A key to the cabin door. It doesn't make you one of us again, so don't get any ideas.
At least you can stop dropping through my ceiling.
Footsteps pound down the stairs. A thief skids to a halt beside the table, gasping for breath.
Boss! It's Piwh! He came stumbling down the road and collapsed at the cabin door. He's burning up, and he can barely breathe.
Piwh? Get him down to the dorm, now! And wake Ysolmere!
The thief runs back up the stairs. Graball stares after him, his beer forgotten.
Piwh is my catchpole. He was tracking something for me, and now this. Ysolmere will need help, and you've got a key now. Get down to the dorm.
Not now! Piwh needs help!
Piwh lies on the bed, pale and drenched in sweat. His breathing is shallow, and he doesn't respond when you speak to him.
Not now. I'm busy.
A woman kneels beside Piwh's bed, pressing a damp cloth to his forehead. She doesn't look up.
You're the one Graball sent? Good. Bring that lamp closer.
Poison. Quill thinks it's a fever, but look at his lips, and the black under his nails. Someone wanted him dead, and slowly.
I can keep him breathing, but not with what I have here. This dorm is stocked for knife cuts and hangovers.
Two Izthiel claws, an Angel feather, two Cyclopea roots, two jars of honey and two Orchard apples.
Deebo grows them, in his orchard northeast of Sullengard. Nothing else cuts the bitterness enough to get the rest down him. Deebo is wary of strangers, though. He only sells to people he trusts.
Which one?
Izthiels lurk along the waterways and the lake shore road. Kill one and take its claws. Not every one has claws worth taking, so you may need to kill a few.

From the Angel of death. It haunts the forest and the graveyard between Vilegard and Sullengard. Folk say a feather under a sick man's pillow calls the Angel to him. Burn one, and its smoke sends the Angel away.
Cyclopea creepers grow in the hills west of Sullengard. Most of them have nothing but rot under them, so you may have to dig up a lot of creepers.
Leofric, the beekeeper just east of the Foaming Flask. He sells it by the jar.
Hurry. I don't know how long he has.
Do you have them? Two Izthiel claws, an Angel feather, two Cyclopea roots, two jars of honey and two Orchard apples.

Ysolmere grinds the claws and roots into a paste and stirs it into the honey and apple pulp. She works a spoonful between Piwh's lips, then holds the feather to the lamp and lets its smoke drift over him.
There. His breathing's steadier. He'll live, as long as he's left to sleep. Go and tell Graball. He'll want to know who did this to his catchpole.
He's sleeping. Don't wake him. Graball will want to hear from you.
Keep your voice down! They came down a rope through the hole in the ceiling, six of them, all in black. One stayed in here. The rest went on toward the vault.
They didn't even look at him. They knew exactly where they were going. Go! I'm not leaving Piwh.
Piwh is asleep. His color has come back, and his breathing is slow and even.
Then why are you here? Whatever Ysolmere needs, get it. Piwh can't wait.
Well? How is he?

replies.text: He'll live. Ysolmere says he was poisoned.

message: Graball sets his mug down, very slowly.
Someone poisoned my catchpole and left him to crawl home. I want to know who, and you're going to find out for me.

Bring me names, or anything that tells me who they are. What happens to them after that is my business.

Birds. Nests, fledglings, crows. It's a code, and not a clever one. The birds are people.
A young one that fell from its nest? That's you, dropping through my ceiling. Whoever wrote this saw you fall, and those two had it from him after they dealt with Piwh.

replies.text: And the old crow on his perch?

message: Bramver. He sits on that hill all day with his eyes on the sky, and on my cabin. He saw you fall and sold it to whoever those two work for. Now they know about the hole.
Quill told me Bramver packed up his camp and rode off. I thought nothing of it. Now I do. Bramver is gone.
Those two weren't working alone. Whoever sent them knows about the hole now, and they'll use it. Go and take a look at it. Quietly.
The hole. Go and look at it before someone else uses it.
Piwh? Of course. He's the only one around here who actually eats my stew. Why?
Poisoned? Not by my stew, I hope! It may smell bad, but it never hurt anyone.
Two days ago. He ate, he talked my ear off, and then he left in a hurry. Two men in black robes got up right after him. They hadn't touched their food.
Toward the Crossroads Guardhouse, all three of them. I remember thinking those two didn't look much like travelers.
They followed Piwh out, toward the Crossroads Guardhouse. That's all I know.
Piwh? Never heard of him. And if I had, I wouldn't tell a stranger. Make yourself useful around here first. Gandoren over there is always looking for someone to run his errands.
Piwh? Maybe I've heard something. But you ran Feygard's errands for them, so you can pay Feygard prices. {5000} gold.
Then go and ask your friends in Feygard. I'm sure they know all about it.
Feygard gold spends as well as any other.
You've already paid, so I suppose I owe you the rest.
Piwh? Talkative fellow, always asking questions? He came through here two days ago.
Not when he arrived. Then two men in black robes walked up, and the three of them stood out by the road, talking quietly. Piwh did most of the listening.

Two men in black robes, and one name: Alynndir. Someone by that name lives along the Duleian Road, east of the Foaming Flask Tavern.

A man running east along the road, and two men in black robes right behind him. That's all I saw.

I walk with the Shadow too. This is none of my business.

message: Then Graball will be disappointed.

The two men slip off the road and into the trees. As they go, a folded scrap of paper falls from the leader's sleeve. You pick it up and unfold it. It's all about birds: a nest in the hills, a fledgling that fell from it, and an old crow who watches from his perch. None of it makes sense to you. Graball should see this.
One of the black-robed men dropped a note.

You unfold the note. It's written in a cramped hand, and it's all about birds: a nest in the hills, a fledgling that fell from it, and an old crow who watches from his perch. None of it makes sense to you. Graball should see this.
Piwh is in the dorm, and Ysolmere is with him. Go and see whether she needs anything.
Alduan's clock. The house in the ravine. My beer is getting warm while you stand there.
Well? What did the birdwatcher have to say?

replies.text: He says he's seen nothing but birds.
He said a young bird fell out of its nest and landed somewhere soft.

message: A bird fell out of its nest. Fascinating. Truly.
A man rides out every day to stare into a ravine, and all he ever sees is birds. I don't believe a word of it.

And I don't believe you either. You've seen my base, my men and my face, and all that keeps your mouth shut is your word. So you're going to do a job for me. Once you've robbed a house for the Guild, going to the guards would put you in the cell next to ours.
As for you, you've worked for the Guild, but you've never worked for me. Before I trust you with what you've seen down here, I want to see how you handle a job.
As for you, you still owe the Guild for that vault. Consider this your first payment.
There's a man named Alduan with a house in the ravine. He spends all day at the orchard, so the place sits empty. There's a clock on his wall. Bring it to me.
I don't care about the clock. I care that you stole it.
A man who works long days keeps a spare key somewhere near the door. Find it.
Out through the cabin, same as before. And when you come back, use the same hole. I don't need two.
Before you reach the stairs, a voice barks from behind the table.
Oi, not that way. Either you talk to the boss, or you take the stairs at the end of the hall and get out.
You again? The boss sent you to talk to Bramver. Until you have, you've got no business down here.
He takes you by the collar, marches you up the stairs and through the cabin, and shoves you out the front door. It locks behind you.
The door is locked tight. You'll need something to open it.
The door is locked, but there's a note...

As usual, I am at the orchard.

~Alduan
Oh, that place. I can hardly remember what it looks like these days.
While looking off to the east as if to ensure that no one is watching or listening.
You know, it's Deebo. He makes us work so hard and for so long, I'm lucky if I even make it home every night and I certainly can't remember the last time I did so in the light.

replies.text: Well, I do like your house.

message: Hey! What are you doing?
No, Lord Geomyr. Yes you. What are you doing?
You don't talk to another person's horse.
Back again? Did you ever climb down to look at that old crate?
Still here? Watch the sky long enough, and you'll see everything worth seeing.
Ah, a visitor! Come to admire the view?

replies.text: Have you noticed anything unusual around the ravine lately?
Have you seen anyone else wandering around up here?
How do you get out here? I heard the Duleian Road is closed.

message: The road, yes. Soldiers everywhere, and not one of them will say why. But my horse knows a trail through the trees. They can close a road, but they can't close a forest!

replies.text: Have you noticed anything unusual around the ravine lately?
Have you seen anyone else wandering around up here?

message: Unusual? Hmm. The swallows are flying low today. That usually means rain.
Only you! Most folk have more sense than to wander out this far. I like it that way. Just me, my horse and the birds.
Nothing but birds, I'm afraid. Though now that you mention it, one of the young ones tumbled out of its nest recently.
Oh, I expect it's fine. It came down somewhere soft, I'd wager. Fledglings are tougher than they look.
Bramver turns back to the ravine, humming to himself.
Beautiful, isn't it? I ride out here every day, and I never tire of the sight. There's something special about this ravine.

replies.text: What do you like about it?

message: Look to the skies! The birds glide above the ravine as though they haven't a care in the world. I could watch them for hours. There's something wonderful about seeing them soar so freely.
Whenever the weather permits! I saddle my horse and ride out from home. There's no better way to spend an afternoon than enjoying the fresh air and watching the world go by.
Nor City. I follow the Duleian Road north each morning to reach this place. It's a pleasant ride, and the journey itself is half the enjoyment!

replies.text: I'm looking for my brother. His name is Andor. Have you seen him in Nor City?

message: Andor? I cannot say I've met him. What does he look like?

replies.text: He looks like me, though he's a couple of years older.

message: Hmm. I'm not sure I've seen him. Though now that you mention it, I feel I may have heard that name somewhere in Nor City.

replies.text: You think you've heard of him?

message: Perhaps! But don't put too much stock in my memory. I'm a poor listener when my mind is elsewhere, and I'm dreadful with names. I could have heard it yesterday and forgotten it by this morning!
Bramver turns his gaze back toward the ravine.
Speaking of things I've noticed around here, there's something rather curious at the bottom of this ravine.
An old crate. I've spotted it down there, but I've never bothered to climb down and investigate. I'm quite content admiring the view from up here!

replies.text: Do you think there's anything inside?

message: Who can say? It could be full of rubbish, or perhaps someone left something interesting behind. There's only one way to find out!
Oh, I've considered it! But scrambling down there isn't quite my idea of a pleasant afternoon. I'd rather spend my time watching the birds.
But if you're feeling adventurous, why not climb down and have a look? Just mind your footing!

Oh! Hello! You look like an adventurer. Are you an adventurer? I'm an adventurer too. Mostly. Sort of.

My name is Ceckapus. Can I ask you something?
Just one thing! Just one, I promise.
You came back! I knew you would. I've been saving up questions.

Oh. Okay. But wait, what about... no, no, that's fine. Go.

I'll just think of more questions while you're gone. Lots more.
Okay. Okay okay okay. I wrote that down. Well, I didn't. I don't have anything to write with. Next question!

Hmm. I'll think about it.

Oh! That reminds me...

Right. Thanks. I think.

Wait, one more thing...

You don't know? Hmm. Then who would know?

...You don't know that either? That's alright. I'll ask you something else.
Oh. That's alright. I'll ask you again later. Maybe you'll know by then.
Really? You look like someone who knows things. Let me try a different question.
Are you sure? Really, really sure?

Hmm. The last person who told me something like that was wrong. Well, I think they were. I didn't actually go and check.

Are you sure?
Can you say that one more time? Slower?

Then why did you say it?! Now I don't know what to believe.

...Let me ask you something else.
The innkeeper? Balon? He looks busy. He gave me a funny look last time. Could you ask him for me?
I'll ask him later. Maybe tomorrow. Do you think he'll be busy tomorrow?
Hildona? The lady in the kitchen? She waved a ladle at me once. I think it was a wave. Could you ask her for me?
What if she says no? What if she says yes, and then I don't like it? Then what?
Do you know where I could get a book? A good one. About... staying alive, I guess.
Arcir? Who's Arcir? Is he nice? Does he lend them out, or do I have to buy them?

replies.text: He's nice enough. Just ask him.

message: Okay. And where is he? Which town did you say?
Fallhaven... where's Fallhaven?
What map? I don't have a map. Where do I get a map? Does Arcir have maps? He has books, so maybe he has maps.

Crossglen! I've heard of Crossglen.

Wait. Where's Crossglen?

Oh! So you could take me there!

...No? Hmm. Will Arcir still be there when I get there? What if he's out?
Those monsters keep hitting me. Every time! Where can I get some good protective equipment?

replies.text: Fayvara in Charwood can teach you how to wear armor properly.
Zaccheria runs an armour shop in Sullengard.
Maybe stop letting them hit you.
Ask the innkeeper if he knows a merchant.

message:
Sullengard! That's not far, is it? Is it?

Will he give me a discount if I tell him I know you?
How do I do that? I can't just stop! Is there someone who teaches that?
Remgard? Is that far? Is it farther than the soldiers' camp?
Will there be monsters on the way? Will they hit me?

But that's the whole problem! I need the armor to get to the armor!

Could you go buy it for me? I'll pay you back. Probably.
Hmm. Do they at least let anyone in? I heard Remgard doesn't let people in.
I keep swinging my sword, but I always miss. And when they swing back, they never miss. Is there someone who could teach me how to fight? Or how to not get hit?

replies.text: Falothen in Charwood teaches people to handle weapons.
Fayvara in Charwood teaches armor and shields.

message: Outside?! Those are the things that keep hitting me!
Charwood... where is Charwood? Is it a town or a forest? It sounds like a forest. I don't like forests.

replies.text: There's a cabin in the forest, northwest of the Foaming Flask.

message:
The Foaming Flask? Is that a tavern? Is it nicer than this one?

Don't tell Balon I asked.
Someone who teaches you how to not get hit? That's exactly what I need! Does she charge much? I only have fourteen gold. Well, eleven. I bought a pie.

replies.text: For the extra lessons she wants gold and Oegyth crystals.

message: Oegyth crystals? What do they look like? Where do they come from? Do they bite?
And when I get there, do I just... ask? What do I say? Could you write it down for me?

replies.text: Just tell them you want to learn.

message: I'm so hungry for a good fish. Not river-mud fish. A good fish. Do you know where I could get some?

replies.text: Remgard sits on a lake. They have plenty of fish.
Mabyn, east of Lake Sutdover, has fish.

message: Mabyn? Is she a fisherman? Fisherwoman? Fisherperson? Does she share?
Where's Lake Sutdover? Is it a big lake? If it's a big lake, how do I find the house? Do I walk around it? Which way?
Remgard? Everyone says Remgard! Is everything in Remgard?

Then why doesn't everyone just live in Remgard?

Do you live in Remgard?
Is the food here any good? What should I order? What do you usually order?
Anything? Even the soup? What's in the soup? Have you seen what's in the soup?

Then how do you know anything is fine?!

...I'll just have bread. Is the bread fine?
Can I sleep here? Is there a bed? Is it a good bed? Do they check it for bugs?

replies.text: I slept here. It was fine.

message: Did anything bite you? Check your arms. Go on, check them.
Is the road safe? The soldiers at the camp kept saying something about an investigation. Am I in trouble? I didn't do anything. I don't think.

replies.text: The road is closed while they investigate. I needed a pass from the sergeant.

message:
A pass? Can I have your pass?

...Why not? Could you get me one? What did you have to do to get it?

replies.text: I convinced the sergeant I could help.

message: Convinced him? How? What did you say? Say it exactly like you said it to him.

replies.text: I told him about a case I solved.

message: They closed the road right after I got here, and now I'm stuck. But you got past the soldiers! They don't let just anyone through. How did you get them to trust you?

replies.text: I solved a murder in Brimhaven.
I found out what happened to the missing people of Remgard.
I solved a murder in Stoutford.
I found out where all the beer at the Foaming Flask was coming from.
I found out where all the beer at the Foaming Flask was coming from.
I found out where all the beer at the Foaming Flask was coming from.
I got a merchant's stolen goods back in Sullengard.

message: A case? You solve cases? What kind of case? Which one?

replies.text: I solved a murder in Brimhaven.
I found out what happened to the missing people of Remgard.
I solved a murder in Stoutford.
I found out where all the beer at the Foaming Flask was coming from.
I found out where all the beer at the Foaming Flask was coming from.
I found out where all the beer at the Foaming Flask was coming from.
I got a merchant's stolen goods back in Sullengard.

message: A murder?! Who did it? Did you catch them? Were you scared? I would have been scared.

replies.text: A man named Ogea did it.

message: Ogea... How did you know it was him? Did he tell you? Did you just ask him?

replies.text: It all started with a strange-looking dagger I bought.

message: You bought a dagger, and it solved a murder? Where can I buy one of those?
Missing people? Where did they go? Did you find them? Were they hiding?

replies.text: A witch named Algangror was behind it.

message: A WITCH?! What did you do?

Dealt with her how? ...No, don't tell me. Yes, tell me. No, don't.

Is she gone? Really gone?
A murder?! Who did it? How did you prove it?

replies.text: Blornvale, the alchemist. He drank a potion of truth and confessed.

message: A potion of truth? That's a real thing? Could I get one? I'd make Balon drink it and ask him what's really in the soup.
Beer? You got past the soldiers because of... beer?

replies.text: Someone was bootlegging it, and I found out who.

message: Bootlegged beer? Is this beer bootlegged? I've had three of these. Should I stop drinking it?
Stolen goods? Did you fight the thieves? Were there a lot of them? Did they have knives?

replies.text: I tracked down the stolen things and returned them to Zaccheria.

message: Zaccheria... What did they steal from him? What does he sell?

replies.text: He runs the armour shop in Sullengard.

message: ARMOUR?! You know an armour seller, and you didn't tell me? I've been asking everyone about armour!
Are you out here all alone? Doesn't your family worry about you?

replies.text: I'm looking for my brother, Andor. My father Mikhail is waiting at home.

message: You lost your brother? How do you lose a brother? Was he very small?

replies.text: He isn't small. He just left.

message: What does he look like?

replies.text: A bit like me, I suppose.

message:
Like you... So he looks like... a person.

I think I saw a person earlier! Wait, no. That was Balon. Was it Balon? Is Balon your brother?
Somebody said children have been going missing around here. Is that true? Should I be worried? I'm not a child. Am I? I'm not, right?

replies.text: Yes. Children have been disappearing near the road.

message:
Who's taking them? Do you know? Are you going to find out? Can I come?

...Actually, no. Can you just tell me afterwards?
A small clock hangs on the wall, ticking away in the empty house. It's the only thing in here worth more than the walls around it.
You lift the clock off its hook. It keeps ticking in your hands, louder than seems fair.
A clean patch on the wall shows where the clock used to hang. Alduan will notice eventually, though he may wonder whether he ever owned a clock at all.
A man who gets home after dark keeps a spare where his hands can find it.
You tip the apple crate back, and there, pressed into the dirt, is a small iron key.
This is where Alduan keeps his spare key. If it were back under the crate, he'd have no reason to think anyone had used it.
You press the key back into the dirt and lower the crate over it, just as you found it.
Alduan's key is back under the crate, right where he left it.
A crate of apples, slowly going soft in the sun.
